ut_castleton_tower.blurb:
The most recognisable tower in the Moab desert and the first big one climbed here, Castleton stands on a long talus cone above Castle Valley: a clean column of Wingate sandstone whose faces carry a hard calcite crust that makes the holds feel almost like granite. The Kor-Ingalls Route on the south face is one of the most repeated climbs in North America, the North Chimney gives a second 5.9 of the same quality, and harder free lines and aid routes take the other faces.

Expect company. On a good spring or fall weekend a line forms at the base of Kor-Ingalls, and the sun moves round the tower through the day, so which face is in shade changes by the hour. Every free route is traditional and sustained for its grade, so climb well within your limits — this is not the place to try a first 5.9. The sandstone is fragile when wet; give it a dry day after rain.
ut_castleton_tower.parking_note: From Moab take Highway 128 along the Colorado River for about 15 miles, then turn right onto Castle Valley Road and follow it roughly 4.5 miles. A quarter to half a mile past the cattle guard, the trailhead lot and a small free campground sit on the left. Park there and start up the wash.
